content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jesus Cooke (E029) requests write access to Source Code.

Notes:
- Note 1 (HR?): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommends write. Says full-time employees may have up to write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommends read. Says contractor without advanced training max out at read.

Conflict: employment type - full_time vs contractor. Note 2 explicitly says Security DB shows contractor (looked up in own database) and points out a discrepancy from the previous note. Note 1 apparently didn't verify employment type as thoroughly? Actually note 1 says "looked up in own database before writing" for employment type. Note 2 also says looked up in own database.

Hmm. Which to trust? Note 2 mentions Security DB shows contractor, not full-time as previously noted. The Security note seems to correct the HR note. The Security agent looked up in own database - security database likely has employment type too.

Policy:
- full_time: up to write (admin only if role owns system; role is Payroll Specialist, Source Code owned by Engineer, so max write anyway).
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → read.

Requested: write.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Grant read (requested write > max, grant max).
If full-time: max is write, grant write.

The conflicting notes. Which evidence to use? The security note explicitly says contractor with basic training, and it corrects the previous note. The security agent looked up employment type in its own database. The HR note says full-time looked up in own database.

Hmm, this is a judgment call. The Security note seems more specific and explicitly addresses the discrepancy, saying "Security DB shows ... contractor (not full-time as previously noted)". That suggests the security database is authoritative for the correction.

I'll grant read, since contractor with basic training maxes at read. The requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
